_meta.about: ANANT.AI first seed batch — 8 real Indian companies, placement-relevant, across quick commerce, fintech, retail, beauty, eyewear and insurtech.
_meta.schema: Matches ARCHITECTURE.md §4. One record per company. Every figure carries a source + period. No figure without a source.
_meta.figure_source_caveat: Figures below are as reported by business media citing company filings / RoC (Registrar of Companies) accounts. BEFORE PRODUCTION, replace each source URL with the exact annual-report or RoC filing PDF and the line-item/page reference. Media-reported numbers are a staging step, not the final citation.
_meta.units: All figures in INR crore (₹ crore). FY = financial year ended 31 March.

companies.name: Eternal (Zomato)

parts.SELLS: The parent of Zomato (food delivery) and Blinkit (10-minute grocery). Also runs Hyperpure (B2B supplies to restaurants) and District (going-out and events).
parts.EARNS: Takes commissions and delivery fees from restaurants, sells ads to them, and earns product margins through Blinkit and Hyperpure. Quick commerce is now the growth engine.
parts.SIZE: FY25 consolidated revenue of about ₹20,243 crore, up 67%, with profit after tax of ₹527 crore.
parts.RIVALS: Swiggy in food delivery; Blinkit competes with Zepto and Swiggy Instamart in quick commerce.
parts.WATCH: How fast Blinkit scales dark stores without burning cash, and whether quick commerce stays profitable as competition intensifies.

source.title: Eternal FY25 Annual Report (reported by Medianama)
Eternal FY25 Annual Report (reported by Medianama)

quiz.prompt: How does Eternal mainly earn from Zomato?
options: Commissions, delivery fees and ads from restaurants

quiz.prompt: Which Eternal business is its quick-commerce arm?

companies.note_30w: Eternal owns Zomato and Blinkit. It earns commissions, delivery fees and ads, plus grocery margins. FY25 revenue near ₹20,243 crore, profit ₹527 crore. Quick commerce is the growth story to watch.

companies.name: Swiggy

parts.SELLS: Food delivery plus Instamart (quick-commerce grocery), dining-out bookings and a pick-up-and-drop service, Genie. Listed on the exchanges in late 2024.
parts.EARNS: Commissions and delivery fees from restaurants, advertising, and product margins through Instamart. Instamart is the big bet and the big cost.
parts.SIZE: FY25 consolidated revenue of about ₹15,227 crore, up 35%, with a net loss of about ₹3,117 crore.
parts.RIVALS: Zomato in food delivery; Instamart competes with Blinkit and Zepto in quick commerce.
parts.WATCH: Whether Instamart's losses narrow as it scales, and the path to profitability now that the company is public.

source.title: Swiggy FY25 results (reported by Indian Retailer)
Swiggy FY25 results (reported by Indian Retailer)

quiz.prompt: What was Swiggy's FY25 position on profit?
options: A net loss of about ₹3,117 crore

companies.note_30w: Swiggy does food delivery plus Instamart quick commerce. It earns commissions, fees and ads. FY25 revenue about ₹15,227 crore but a net loss near ₹3,117 crore. Watch Instamart's path to profit.

companies.name: Zepto

parts.SELLS: A quick-commerce app promising grocery and essentials in about ten minutes, run through a network of small local warehouses called dark stores.
parts.EARNS: Product margins on what it sells, plus delivery and handling fees, platform charges and advertising from brands. Dark-store density drives the economics.
parts.SIZE: Revenue of about ₹11,110 crore in FY25 (from its RoC filing); net loss of about ₹1,249 crore in FY24.
parts.RIVALS: Blinkit (Eternal), Swiggy Instamart, and BigBasket's quick-commerce push.
parts.WATCH: Whether dark-store unit economics turn positive as it scales, how fast losses narrow, and its reported move toward an IPO.

source.title: Zepto FY25 RoC filing (reported by Entrackr)
Zepto FY24 RoC filing (reported by Entrackr)

quiz.prompt: What is a 'dark store' in Zepto's model?
options: A small local warehouse for fast delivery

quiz.prompt: How does Zepto make money beyond product margins?
options: Delivery and handling fees, plus ads from brands

companies.note_30w: Zepto is ten-minute quick commerce built on dark stores. It earns product margins, delivery and handling fees, and brand ads. FY25 revenue about ₹11,110 crore. Watch dark-store economics and a possible IPO.

companies.name: Avenue Supermarts (DMart)

parts.SELLS: A value-retail chain of large DMart stores selling groceries, staples, household goods, apparel and general merchandise at low everyday prices.
parts.EARNS: Thin retail margins on huge volumes. It keeps costs low by owning most stores rather than renting, and turning inventory quickly.
parts.SIZE: FY25 net sales of about ₹53,333 crore, with net profit of about ₹2,707 crore.
parts.RIVALS: Reliance Retail, local kirana stores, and online and quick-commerce grocery players.
parts.WATCH: How value retail holds up against quick commerce for grocery, and how fast it grows DMart Ready, its online arm.

source.title: Avenue Supermarts FY25 Annual Report (analysis, Equitymaster)
Avenue Supermarts FY25 Annual Report (analysis, Equitymaster)

options: Owning most stores and turning inventory fast

quiz.prompt: DMart's model is best described as:
options: Value retail at low everyday prices

companies.note_30w: DMart is value retail: large stores, low everyday prices, thin margins on big volumes. It owns most stores and turns inventory fast. FY25 net sales about ₹53,333 crore, profit ₹2,707 crore.

companies.name: Nykaa (FSN E-Commerce)

parts.SELLS: An online retailer of beauty and personal care, plus a fashion arm. It stocks and sells products directly and also runs owned brands and physical stores.
parts.EARNS: Product margins on beauty it holds as inventory, commissions on marketplace items, advertising from brands, and higher margins on its own private labels.
parts.SIZE: FY25 revenue of about ₹7,950 crore, up 24%, with net profit of about ₹72 crore.
parts.RIVALS: Tira (Reliance), Myntra Beauty, Purplle, and Amazon and Flipkart's beauty sections.
parts.WATCH: Whether the fashion business turns profitable, and how it defends beauty against Tira's well-funded push.

source.title: FSN E-Commerce FY25 results (reported by Apparel Resources)
FSN E-Commerce FY25 results (reported by Apparel Resources)

quiz.prompt: Why can Nykaa's beauty margins differ from a pure marketplace?
options: It holds beauty as inventory and sells private labels

quiz.prompt: Who is a major new rival in beauty for Nykaa?

companies.note_30w: Nykaa sells beauty online, holding inventory and owning brands, plus a fashion arm. It earns product margins, commissions, ads and private-label margins. FY25 revenue about ₹7,950 crore, profit ₹72 crore. Watch Tira's challenge.

companies.name: Paytm (One97 Communications)

parts.SELLS: Digital payments for consumers and merchants — QR codes, soundboxes and card machines — plus distribution of financial services like loans and insurance.
parts.EARNS: Margins on payment processing, subscriptions and rentals on merchant devices, and commissions for distributing loans and other financial products.
parts.SIZE: FY25 revenue of about ₹6,900 crore (down 31%), with net loss narrowing to about ₹663 crore.
parts.RIVALS: PhonePe and Google Pay in payments; BharatPe among merchants.
parts.WATCH: The reshaped lending model, fallout from the Paytm Payments Bank wind-down, and the timeline to steady profit.

source.title: One97 Communications FY25 results (reported by The Head and Tale)
One97 Communications FY25 results (reported by The Head and Tale)

quiz.prompt: Besides payments, how does Paytm earn?
options: Device rentals and distributing loans and insurance

quiz.prompt: Who are Paytm's main payment rivals?

companies.note_30w: Paytm runs consumer and merchant payments with QR, soundboxes and devices, and distributes loans and insurance. FY25 revenue about ₹6,900 crore, loss narrowing to ₹663 crore. Watch the lending reset and profit timeline.

companies.name: Lenskart

parts.SELLS: Eyewear — spectacles, lenses and sunglasses — sold both online and through a large store network, under its own brands including Lenskart and John Jacobs.
parts.EARNS: Product margins on frames and lenses, widened by making much of its own eyewear, plus a membership plan. Omnichannel reach drives volume.
parts.SIZE: FY24 revenue of about ₹5,427 crore, with a small net loss of about ₹10 crore (from its RoC filing).
parts.RIVALS: Titan Eyeplus, independent opticians, and other online eyewear brands.
parts.WATCH: Store expansion in India and abroad (Southeast Asia and the Middle East), and margins as it scales after going public.

source.title: Lenskart FY24 RoC filing (reported by Entrackr)
Lenskart FY24 RoC filing (reported by Entrackr)

quiz.prompt: What widens Lenskart's margins versus a pure reseller?
options: It makes much of its own eyewear
Omnichannel — online and a large store network

companies.note_30w: Lenskart sells eyewear online and through many stores, under its own brands, making much of its product to widen margins. FY24 revenue about ₹5,427 crore, near break-even. Watch store expansion and overseas growth.

companies.name: PB Fintech (Policybazaar)

parts.SELLS: Runs Policybazaar, an online marketplace to compare and buy insurance, and Paisabazaar, a marketplace for loans and credit products.
parts.EARNS: Commissions from insurers on policies sold, lead-generation and distribution fees, and newer lines like its agent platform and healthcare push.
parts.SIZE: FY25 revenue of about ₹4,977 crore, with net profit of about ₹345 crore.
parts.RIVALS: Insurers' own websites, banks, and direct digital insurers such as Acko and Digit.
parts.WATCH: Spending on new initiatives, insurance regulation, and how fast higher-margin health insurance grows.

source.title: PB Fintech FY25 results (reported by The Head and Tale)
PB Fintech FY25 results (reported by The Head and Tale)

options: Commissions from insurers and distribution fees

companies.note_30w: PB Fintech runs Policybazaar for insurance and Paisabazaar for loans. It earns insurer commissions and distribution fees. FY25 revenue about ₹4,977 crore, profit ₹345 crore. Watch new-initiative spend and health-insurance growth.
